latest_nl_proof:
Let m = floor(nr). Since n > 1, in particular n is positive. From 0 <= r, multiplying by the positive সংখ্যা n gives 0 <= nr. Because m = floor(nr) is the greatest integer less than or equal to nr, and 0 is an integer with 0 <= nr, it follows that m >= 0.

Also, since r < 1 and n > 0, multiplying by n gives nr < n. Again by the floor property, m <= nr, so m < n.

Therefore 0 <= m < n, as required.
role_in_parent: Ensures the cell index m is in the range covered by the cellwise property of f_n.
statement_nl: Under the hypotheses n > 1, 0 <= r < 1, and m = floor(n*r), the integer m satisfies 0 <= m < n.

domain_restrictions: m is defined as floor of n*r (so m is an integer and equals the greatest integer less than or equal to n*r)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers n and all real numbers r with n > 1 and 0 <= r < 1, if m is defined by m = floor(n*r), then 0 <= m and m < n.
